problems.title: Shift a geometric sum by one term
problems.question: Four geometric terms have first-three sum 29 and last-three sum 58. Find their ratio.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
formulas: The last-three sum equals the first-three sum multiplied by $q$.
steps: $58=29q$ gives $q=2$. The nonzero first sum permits division.

problems.title: A quotient of distant geometric terms
problems.question: $b_1=1,b_2=2$. Evaluate $(b_{2021}+b_{2019})/(b_{2021}-b_{2019})$.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: Cancel the positive common factor $b_{2019}$ to get $(4+1)/(4-1)=5/3$.

problems.title: An alternating reciprocal sequence
problems.question: $a_1=1/3$, $a_{n+1}=1/a_n$. Find a formula for $a_n$.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
formulas: Taking a reciprocal twice restores the original positive number.
steps: The sequence repeats $1/3,3,1/3,3,\ldots$.
For odd $n$, $(-1)^n=-1$, while for even $n$ it is 1. Thus $3^{(-1)^n}$ gives exactly these values.

problems.title: Coefficients of an internal-division vector
problems.question: $AM:MC=1:4$ and $BM=xBA+yBC$ as vectors. Find $x-y$.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: Subtract $B$ to get $BM=(4/5)BA+(1/5)BC$.
The coefficient difference is $4/5-1/5=3/5$.

problems.title: A quotient of commutative dot products
problems.question: $ABCD$ is a nonrectangular parallelogram. Find $(AB\cdot BC)/(AD\cdot DC)$ using vectors.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: The numerator and denominator are equal. The nonrectangular condition ensures adjacent side vectors are not perpendicular, so the common dot product is nonzero.

problems.title: An index relation in an arithmetic progression
problems.question: A nonconstant arithmetic progression satisfies $a_3+a_n=a_1+a_{11}$. Find $n$.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: Substitute: $2a_1+(n+1)d=2a_1+10d$.
Cancel the common terms and divide by $d$ to obtain $n+1=10$, so $n=9$.

problems.title: Recover a geometric sequence from sums
problems.question: The first-$n$ sum of a geometric sequence is $S_n=3^n-1$. Find its common ratio.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: $a_n=3^n-3^{n-1}=2\cdot3^{n-1}$. Consecutive terms therefore have ratio 3.

problems.title: Two-digit integers with remainder two
problems.question: How many two-digit natural numbers leave remainder 2 on division by 7?
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
formulas: The values form an arithmetic progression with difference 7.
steps: The first is 16 and last 93. Their count is $(93-16)/7+1=12$.

problems.title: Expand a dot product bilinearly
problems.question: $|a|=|b|=1$ and their angle is $60^\circ$. Find $(a+2b)\cdot(2a+b)$.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: Expansion gives $2|a|^2+5a\cdot b+2|b|^2=2+5/2+2=13/2$.

problems.title: A vector combination in coordinates
problems.question: $a=(1,2),b=(2,1),c=(2,2)$ and $c=xa+yb$. Find $x+y$.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
formulas: Equality of vectors means equality of both coordinates.
steps: The equations are $x+2y=2$ and $2x+y=2$. Add them: $3(x+y)=4$.

problems.title: Opposite terms in an arithmetic progression
problems.question: $a_1=7$ and $a_{10}=-a_{20}$. Find the common difference.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.

problems.title: The closest integer to a quadratic vertex
problems.question: For $a_n=(n-19.9)^2+199$, which listed term is smallest?
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
formulas: The squared distance from 19.9 is smallest at the nearest integer index.
steps: 20 is distance 0.1 from 19.9; every other integer index is farther. Thus $a_{20}$ is smallest.

problems.title: A finite sum just below an infinite sum
problems.question: A geometric progression has first term 3 and ratio $1/4$. Which listed interval contains its first-60 sum?
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: $S_{60}=4(1-4^{-60})<4$. It exceeds 3 because the first term is 3 and all later terms are positive.

problems.title: Use perpendicularity to find a vector length
problems.question: $(x,-8)$ is perpendicular to $(2,4)$. Find its length.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
formulas: Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero.
steps: $2x-32=0$ gives $x=16$. The length is $\sqrt{16^2+8^2}=\sqrt{320}=8\sqrt5$.

problems.title: Cosine between coordinate vectors
problems.question: $a=(1,0),b=(0,1)$. Find the cosine between $2a+b$ and $a+3b$.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: The vectors are $(2,1),(1,3)$, with dot product 5 and lengths $\sqrt5,\sqrt{10}$.
The cosine is $5/\sqrt{50}=\sqrt2/2$.

problems.title: Product of two hundred geometric terms
problems.question: First term is 1 and ratio 3. Find $b_1b_2\cdots b_{200}$.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: The product adds the exponents to 19900.

problems.title: An odd power determines a negative ratio
problems.question: $b_{10}=30,b_{19}=-70$. Find the real common ratio.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: $q^9=-70/30=-7/3$. An odd power has a unique real inverse, so $q=-(7/3)^{1/9}$.

problems.title: A proportional list with a known total
problems.question: $a_1,\ldots,a_{10}$ are proportional to $2,3,\ldots,11$ and total 13. Find $a_4$.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: $65k=13$, so $k=1/5$. The fourth term corresponds to 5, giving $a_4=1$.

problems.title: A vector sum along a trapezoid
problems.question: Trapezoid bases $BC,AD$ have lengths 3,6, and vector $BC=a$. Find $AB+CD$.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: The base vectors have the same direction, so $AD=2a$. Subtract $BC=a$ to get $AB+CD=a$.

problems.title: Length of a weighted vector sum
problems.question: $|a|=1,|b|=2$, and their angle is $60^\circ$. Find $|2a+3b|$.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: $a\cdot b=1\cdot2\cos60^\circ=1$. Thus the squared length is $4+36+12=52$.

problems.title: Read the vertex form of a parabola
problems.question: Find the vertex of $y=2(x-3)^2+4$.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: Here $h=3,k=4$. The square vanishes at $x=3$, giving vertex ordinate 4.

problems.title: Maximum area with a fixed leg sum
problems.question: A right triangle’s legs total 14. What is its largest possible area?
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: $ab\le49$, so area $ab/2\le49/2=24.5$. Equality occurs when both legs are 7.

problems.title: A sign chart for a rational quadratic
problems.question: Solve $(x^2-5x+4)/(x^2-5x+6)<0$.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: Critical values are 1,2,3,4. The quotient is negative on $(1,2)$ and $(3,4)$ and positive on the other intervals.
Numerator zeros are excluded by strictness and denominator zeros are undefined.

problems.title: A midpoint vector in a parallelogram
problems.question: $K$ is the midpoint of $BC$, $AB=b$, $AK=k$ as vectors. Find $DK$.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
steps: Thus $v=2(k-b)$. Subtract $AD$ from $AK$: $DK=k-v=2b-k$.

problems.title: Area of a quadrilateral inside a unit square
problems.question: A unit square has $M$ the midpoint of $AD$ and $N$ the midpoint of $BM$. Find $[CDMN]$.
problems.idea: Apply the governing formula and verify any restrictions or special cases.
formulas: Coordinate polygon area is half the absolute shoelace sum.
steps: For $C,D,M,N$, the forward shoelace sum is $3/2$ and backward sum $1/2$. The area is $(3/2-1/2)/2=1/2$.
